Subject: Proposed changes to Order Form & required flow-down

Hi Jonas / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudFleet is excited to move forward. Attached is our latest Order Form with a few requested redlines (CF_OrderForm_v2_redlines.docx) plus an updated Attachment A (SOW) that includes a short subcontracting paragraph.

Key asks from our side:
- Flow-down of data protection obligations to any subprocessor that will handle telemetry or production logs. We proposed specific language in Clause 5.3 (see doc).
- A carve-in allowing us to require a SOC 2 report for any new subprocessor with access to customer data.
- Procure a subprocessor list and notify us 30 days before onboarding new vendors.

Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept the proposed flow-down text or if you require an alternate DPA route? Also please share the standard subprocessor addendum you use for order forms.

I've CC'd Emily (external counsel) who will be on standby for any legal clarifications.

Attachments: CF_OrderForm_v2_redlines.docx; CF_SOW_AttachmentA.pdf

Thanks,
Sam Patel
Contracts Manager
CloudFleet Solutions

Sam — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. We're keen to keep momentum.

Lauren / Markus — looping you both in to triage the proposed flow-down language. High-level plan:
- Legal to confirm whether the proposed Clause 5.3 is materially different from our standard DPA flow-down (I suspect we can accept with a narrow amendment).
- If needed, propose a short alternative clause that preserves CloudFleet's SOC 2 requirement but avoids vendor-level notification windows that conflict with our procurement cadence.
- Schedule a 30-minute call with CloudFleet + Emily tomorrow for quick alignment.

Sam — are you available for a 30-min slot tomorrow (Fri 11/6) between 10–12 PST? If so we’ll send a calendar invite and attach our standard Subprocessor Addendum and a redline.

Best,
Jonas
VP, Partnerships (on behalf of Redwood Inference)
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed changes to Order Form & required flow-down

Jonas / Markus — quick pass from Legal below. Quoting the vendor: 

> "Vendor shall flow down to its subcontractors all data protection obligations in this Agreement; Vendor shall provide Customer with a list of Subprocessors at least 30 days prior to engagement and provide SOC 2 reports on request."

Concerns and suggested edits:
- 30-day notification for every subprocessor is operationally heavy and could block patch-level contractors (e.g., monitoring providers). Suggest: require notification only for subprocessors that will process production customer data (not infra/infra-ops).
- SOC 2 "on request" is broad; propose limiting to SOC 2 Type II for subprocessors that have access to production telemetry or customer PII, and allow receipt of a redacted SOC 2 if full report is restricted by third-party NDA.
- Add a mutual acknowledgement that for short-term or emergency vendors (outage response) Redwood will provide post-hoc notice and remediation commitments rather than pre-approval.

Proposed substitute language (high level):
"For any Subprocessor that will access Customer Production Data, Vendor will: (i) provide Customer written notice at least 30 days prior to onboarding (or as soon as practicable for emergency engagements); (ii) make available to Customer a current SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent security attestation (redactions allowed where necessary); and (iii) flow down obligations materially equivalent to those in this Agreement."

I'll attach our annotated DPA and a short redline for the Order Form (RW_DPA_annotations.pdf). If Markus concurs, I can send the redline to CloudFleet and loop Emily for any follow-ups.

-Lauren
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Data Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachments: RW_DPA_annotations.pdf
From: Emily Morgan <emily.morgan@mwlaw.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@cloudfleet.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed changes to Order Form & required flow-down

Hi all — quick note from external counsel after reviewing Lauren's suggested language. I agree with the narrower operational carve-outs and the SOC 2 limitation to Type II for subprocessors with production access. A couple of clarifications for the redline before sign-off:

1) Evidence delivery format — CloudFleet should be OK with a redacted SOC 2 report or a written attestation from the subprocessor's auditor confirming the scope. We recommend adding a short line stating that redactions do not defeat the attestation's sufficiency.

2) Emergency response — suggest we add a 7-day post-notification requirement for emergency engagements (Redwood to notify Customer within 7 days and provide remediation steps).

3) Order Form signature flow — to keep the timeline tight, we can accept the revised Order Form via DocuSign provided the Subprocessor Addendum is attached and referenced in the Order Form body.

Please confirm if Redwood can produce a current subprocessor list and the SOC 2 evidence for the handful of production-facing vendors (we can accept redacted). I'll coordinate final language with Contracts on CloudFleet's side once we have your list and the attached documents.

Best regards,
Emily Morgan
Partner, Morgan & Wells LLP
(emily.morgan@mwlaw.com)

Attachment: SOC2_Redacted.pdf
